title: Vulcan failure caused by inadequate fuel supply to engines, ULA says
gist: ULA's preliminary review found the Vulcan Leo 1 launch failure stemmed from inadequate fuel supply from the vehicle to the BE-4 engines, not engine performance, clearing Blue Origin's New Glenn to pursue a January return to flight and relieving NASA. For cash-strapped ULA, a new propellant plumbing problem means months offline and competitive erosion amid a US launch crunch.

insights.claim: ULA's initial integrated review indicates Vulcan's low booster thrust on the Leo 1 launch came from inadequate fuel supply from the vehicle to the BE-4 engines, not from engine performance.
insights.speaker: Eric Berger
insights.so_what: Shifts failure responsibility from Blue Origin to ULA's vehicle design.
insights.quote: preliminary indications are that the low booster thrust was the result of inadequate fuel supply from the vehicle to the BE-4 engines, not from the performance of the engines

insights.claim: The Centaur V upper stage did not contribute to the failure, a relief to NASA, which recently contracted ULA to use Centaur V as the new upper stage of the Space Launch System.
